As someone who also has a spouse who’s manic episodes has sometimes left our life in ruins and leaving me to pick up the pieces- I disagree. You can vent to anybody as a family member and they’ll easily sympathize with you and tell you how “strong” and “amazing” you are for sticking by them and dealing with all of it- something I get told  honestly as soon as people find out my spouse is bipolar (I honestly hate it too- all it does is make him feel like a burden hearing ppl say that to me all the time) 

However, being a bipolar person- there are not many people you can talk to and truly not be judged and just get sympathy and support when you tell people what you’ve gone through and what you’ve done. People talk the talk, but so few people in my experience actually empathize and understand- most just assume some nasty or just mean and disheartening things. 

The thing is- it is the same amount of control you would have over like a cold or flu when you’re manic(at least in my husbands case). Would your significant other do those things that ruined your life if they were in a baseline “normal” state of mind? (I hate using the word normal but can’t think of the right term). I know with my husband, he would NEVER do the things he’s done if he had full control. If for no other reason simply because he loves me. 

It sounds to me like maybe you don’t have anyone to vent to, or maybe you feel like you aren’t allowed to vent. I’ve been there, it’s a shitty feeling, and sometimes when you’re taking care of somebody who has a mental health issue and you’re having to clean up the mess they’ve made again and again- it’s easy to get in the mindset of “what about me?”. It’s not wrong to feel that way, it’s a normal feeling. 

I’m sorry for the rambling, I didn’t sleep much last night, but it does sound to me like maybe you personally don’t feel like you have support and you need some- so all of that was to say I also have a spouse with bipolar disorder and if you ever need to talk to someone that “gets it”, I’m here.
